title: Client Fidelity Control Plane and Tool Handshake Playbook
abstract: A pragmatic PRD sketch that defines a lightweight client-side fidelity control plane and handshake protocol for incremental streaming + tool-calling flows. Purpose: reduce wasted tokens, enable graceful low-bandwidth fallbacks, and make structured output contracts observable and debuggable from SDKs.
context_and_problem_statement: We ship many streaming and tool-calling patterns but client behavior is ad-hoc: SDKs either request full fidelity responses (costly) or aggressively degrade without coordinated signal to the server and tools. This causes token waste in hosted mode, mismatches in tool expectations, and poor developer ergonomics for embedding clients with variable networks and quota constraints.
goals: Define a small control-plane API that lets SDKs express desired fidelity lanes (e.g., full, summary-only, outline-first) and preflight tool intents.
Ensure tool adapters (server-side) can advertise capability profiles and minimal preconditions during handshake.
Provide deterministic partial output checkpoints so clients can resume or re-request higher fidelity without duplicating compute or tokens.
Add telemetry hooks to measure end-to-end fidelity transitions and token delta for billing/debugging.
Ship ergonomic SDK primitives for common client platforms (node, browser, mobile) with sensible defaults and easy opt-in overrides.
non_goals: Replace all existing stream formats — this is an incremental compatibility layer.
Attempt full language-model-driven fidelity negotiation (out of scope for initial ship).
Redesign billing model — we expose signals for billing but do not change pricing in this PRD.
user_stories: As a mobile app developer, I want the SDK to request a low-bandwidth summary first, then upgrade to full output if user taps 'See full result', without recharging the user for the initial tokens.
As a platform engineer, I want to see per-request fidelity transitions in the console so I can correlate regressions to model changes.
As an integrator building code execution tooling, I want the server tool-adaptor to declare 'fast-check' vs 'full-run' modes so the model can pick the cheapest viable path.
As an SDK consumer, I want a predictable fallback when a tool is offline (e.g., return an annotated stub result) so my UI doesn't freeze.
As a debugging engineer, I want a compact checkpoint id I can paste into a support ticket to replay the exact partial output state.
control_plane_primitives: Fidelity lanes: string enum {high, medium, low, stub}. Clients propose a lane in the initial request metadata.
Preflight intents: short list of tool ids + estimated budget hint (ms or tokens) to let server choose fast adapters.
Checkpoint frames: server emits stable checkpoint ids with minimal KV (checkpoint_id, cursor_pos, fidelity_lane, partial_summary) to allow resume/upgrade.
Upgrade handshake: clients call /v1/upgrade with checkpoint_id + target_lane to request delta tokens only.
Tool capability descriptors: adapters respond to preflight with "capabilities" list (e.g., supports-fast-check:true, estimated-latency-ms:120) and a suggested fallback.
Telemetry envelope: per-request fidelity events: requested_lane -> negotiated_lane -> upgrades -> final_lane (with timestamps and token counts).
sdk_primitives_and_ergonomics: Client API: generate(options) -> returns an AsyncIterator of events (negotiation, checkpoint, chunk, error, finish).
Convenience: generate().firstSummary() returns the first checkpoint partial_summary as a simple string for low-latency UIs.
Upgrade flow: checkpoint.upgrade(targetLane, opts) performs /v1/upgrade and yields delta chunks only — SDK hides repeated prompt management.
Backpressure: SDK exposes a backoff hook so app-level logic (e.g., UI) can pause streaming while preserving server-side checkpoint state.
Mobile defaults: initial lane=low, checkpoint_policy=enabled, preflight_timeout=200ms to avoid long stalls.
Server-suggested lane acceptance: SDK accepts server negotiated lane unless forceLane=true in options (explicit developer action).
Small stable id: checkpoint ids are base62 16-char strings to be copied in tickets without leaking PII.
Debug tooling: SDK can attach a condensed event log (up to N events) to requests when debug_flag=true for support flows.
structured_output_guidelines: Prefer envelope-first responses: produce a small JSON envelope at first checkpoint with typed slots for summary, actions[], tool_calls[].
Tool-call contracts: each tool_call in the envelope must include schema_version and minimal input/expected_output hints so client UI can render placeholders.
Schema evolution: add a content_hash and schema_version to the checkpoint envelope to support offline diffs and fallback heuristics.
Partial-JSON streaming: server may stream chunks that are either plain text or JSON delta patches; SDK must buffer until a complete JSON object is observed, then emit structured event.
Annotation policy: ambiguous or low-fidelity output must be annotated with "confidence: low" in the envelope to help clients avoid showing overconfident assertions.
Size guidance: initial checkpoint envelope should be <= 1KB to keep first-paint cheap for mobile UIs.
tool_call_protocol_details: Handshake step: client sends tools[] with intents and budgets. Server picks an adapter and returns adapter_profile_id and suggested mode (e.g., fast-check vs full-run). Adapter may accept a temporary stub token that allows limited ops. Tool call sequence should be idempotent: each tool invocation carries a tool_call_id. If a client upgrades, server must be able to resume the adapter run from the last checkpoint without re-running expensive steps when possible. Example tool_call fragment: { tool_call_id: 'tc_42', adapter: 'sql-lite-quick', mode: 'fast-check', stub: true }
observability_and_metrics: Per-request fidelity timeline histogram (requested -> negotiated -> final).
Token delta by lane (tokens used in low vs high lanes for same prompt template).
Tool adapter fallback rate and average additional latency when upgrading.
Checkpoint hit rate (clients that upgrade vs clients that finish at first checkpoint).
SDK-side: percent of requests using checkpoint.upgrade API and error surface for resume failures.
Console surfaces: allow filtering by adapter_profile_id and checkpoint_id to debug live incidents.
rollout_and_migration_plan: Phase 0 (experiment): implement control plane in a beta region, opt-in by SDK flag debug_fidelity=true. Collect telemetry and iterate on icons and UX.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of new hosted-api keys with server-side switch, provide console beta dashboard and sample logs. Ship Node and Browser SDK helpers.
Phase 2 (gradual): default to checkpoint_policy=enabled for mobile SDKs with metrics gating based on 7-day checkpoint hit rate and upgrade success > 95%.
Phase 3 (GA): document stable API, add adapter profile registry for third-party tool integrations, promote SDK helpers to stable packages.
Rollback: server has a flag force_lane=high to bypass negotiation for customer-critical flows during incidents.
security_and_privacy_considerations: Checkpoint ids must not encode PII — strip message content, only include stable minimal metadata.
Tool adapter capability responses must not reveal internal topology; restrict to boolean capability flags and coarse latency buckets.
Telemetry sampling default is 1% for production to avoid exfiltrating user-generated content; support increased sampling for eligible debug requests with consent.
Upgrades require the same auth context — prevent checkpoint hijack by binding checkpoint_id to requester_key hash.
implementation_notes_for_backend_and_run: Runtime: lightweight in-memory checkpoint store with TTL 48h, backed by durable blob storage for long-running jobs.
Serving runtime change: emit negotiation event early in pipeline to avoid unnecessary token generation when lanes disagree.
Adapter contract: adapters implement two APIs: fast_probe(intent, budget) -> capability_hint and resume(run_id, cursor) -> delta_output.
Metrics: add checkpoint_id tag to request traces and a small telemetry header X-Checkpoint-ID for downstream logs.
Backward compatibility: if client doesn't send fidelity headers, server defaults to high lane to preserve current behavior.
open_questions_and_risks: Billing semantics: how to present partial checkpoints in billing dashboards? (Charge final tokens only vs charge incremental).
Complexity: risk of SDK fragmentation if each platform implements slightly different upgrade semantics.
Adapter resume guarantees: not all tools can resume cheaply — need clear adapter opt-out (resume_supported=false).
User expectations: frontends might surface 'partial' as final if not careful; need clear UI guidance and sample components.
Replayability: how long do we keep checkpoint state for enterprise customers with long-running flows? (configurable TTL?)
next_steps_and_action_items: Eng: prototype negotiation + checkpoint events in the streaming gateway (HD-1123) — 2 sprint spike.
SDK: design AsyncIterator ergonomics and firstSummary() helper for node/browser — ship experimental package.
Product: define console dashboard fields and create a support workflow to accept checkpoint ids.
Research: run 1-week A/B test on token-savings between initial-lane=low vs default-high across mobile prompts.
Legal/Security: vet telemetry sampling and checkpoint binding approach for enterprise compliance.
